decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach to the left-side basket; raise and tip gripper gradually, right arm remains parked.
Move left wrist above the basket while completing a downward approach orientation, keeping clearance before descent.
Align over the basket's left egg and descend with open fingers; estimate fingertip offset from the observed wrist and head views.
Fine-align around the left egg, close the left gripper, and pause before testing retention.
Maintain fully closed command and lift vertically to check whether the first egg is retained.
First lift did not retain an egg. Reopen and descend deeper around the left egg with a small lateral correction.
Center the left egg between fingertips, fully close, then make a small retention-test lift.
Hold the pose and fully closed target to let the left fingers settle around the egg; grasp is not yet visually confirmed.
Reposition clear of the basket rim toward the near-center egg with open fingers, then lower cautiously.
Tracking was impeded near the rim. Lift vertically from the observed pose before attempting another lateral approach.
Corrected unexecuted tensor: shift over the near-center egg while high, with narrower fingers for rim clearance.
Descend over the near egg with narrowed fingers, keeping the wrist orientation continuous and monitoring rim clearance.
Close fully around the centered near egg, pause, and lift slightly to verify retention.
Lift the near egg clear while keeping the gripper closed, then start moving toward the holder without crossing the arms.
The near egg was not retained. Reposition above its new location for a deeper grasp, keeping the fingers open and clear of the rim.
Follow the settled near egg slightly left and forward, lowering to a deeper pinch height before closing.
Adjust toward the near egg visible below the fingertips, then close fully while holding the wrist still.
Egg remains below the pinch plane. Reopen and align slightly right and nearer, then lower the fingers around its sides before closing.
Test the current pinch by lifting straight up with the fully closed target; retention must be confirmed visually.
The egg slipped. Move the open pinch farther toward the near edge while descending, using the wrist image to correct the longitudinal offset.
Lift clear of contact, then re-center above the egg that rolled to the right side of the basket; use wrist-camera alignment before another descent.
Lower around the re-centered right-side egg; keep fingers open and approach without lateral contact.
Close on the centered egg, allow the pinch to settle, then perform a slow vertical retention test.
Correct the pinch longitudinally toward the egg and descend slightly with open fingers, rather than lifting an unconfirmed grasp.
Seat the fingers slightly deeper around the visible egg, close fully, and begin a small straight lift.
Lift vertically with a closed gripper to determine whether the egg is now captured between the finger pads.
The egg appears retained above the basket. Keep the grip closed and move toward the central holder with clearance.
The egg slipped back into the basket. Switch to the back egg and restore a vertical pinch orientation before approaching deeper away from the near rim.
Descend vertically above the back egg, keeping the narrower opening clear of the basket sides.
Close around the back egg now centered between the pads; settle and lift slowly without rotating.
Egg appears centered and retained after the small lift. Continue a gentle lift and begin a slow transfer with the gripper fully closed.
Retained egg is stable in the wrist view. Transfer slowly toward the holder at a clear height without rotating the grasp.
Approach the back-left holder cup; gently angle the held egg toward the center while keeping the left wrist on its side and right arm parked.
Lower the retained egg into the back-left cup, with a small rightward alignment correction and the gripper kept closed.
The egg is aligned above the back-left cup; release without pressing against the lid, then withdraw to observe seating.
One egg is visible seated in the holder. Return above the basket's left egg and restore the successful downward pinch orientation.
Align with the remaining left egg and descend to the successful pinch height, maintaining a vertical approach.
Close the centered left egg, settle slightly deeper as the fingers clear the rim, then test a gentle lift.
Keep the closed pinch stable and lift the second egg clear before a slow transfer toward the holder.
Second egg remains between the pads. Transfer toward the front-left cup, angling the gripper rightward while the wrist stays in the left workspace.
Guide the retained second egg down over the front-left cup, correcting rightward and slightly away from the robot.
Lower the second egg into the front-left cup, open the fingers, and withdraw vertically to verify it stays seated.
Two eggs are visible in the left cups. Clear the holder, then move above the farther of the two remaining basket eggs with a vertical pinch.
Center the farther remaining egg using the wrist view and descend with open fingers, avoiding the adjacent egg.
Fine-center the third egg between the pads, close completely, and test a gentle vertical lift.
Lift the third egg slowly with the gripper closed and begin clearing the basket toward the holder.
Transfer the third egg toward the back-right cup, gently tilting the fingers toward the holder while keeping the left wrist left of center and the right arm parked.
Third egg slipped near the holder during tilting. Clear the left arm back over the basket and initialize the right arm to recover it from its own side.
Approach the last basket egg with the left arm while bringing the right arm above the fallen egg in front of the holder; maintain clear separation.
Close the last basket egg at the established pinch height. Align the right gripper above the fallen egg with a downward approach, keeping both arms separated.
Lift the last basket egg slowly on the left. Descend the right gripper around the fallen egg, compensating for its lower table height and leftward offset.
Left egg was not retained; reapproach its nearer position. Shift the right pinch away from the holder lip to center the fallen egg, then close and settle.
Test right-hand retention by a gentle straight lift. The last basket egg rolled left; lift the left fingers clear and re-center before descending again.
Keep the right egg vertical and lift over the holder lip before moving toward the front-right cup. Lower and close the left fingers around the centered final basket egg.
Lift the final basket egg vertically with the left gripper closed. Guide the recovered right egg over the front-right cup and begin lowering without changing its orientation.
Open and withdraw the right gripper to let the third egg settle in the front-right cup. Re-center the left approach on the final egg after its slip.
Three eggs are seated. Fine-align the final egg with the left finger pads and close; move the open right gripper aside for clearance.
Lift the final egg slowly with the left gripper fully closed; keep both orientations fixed and verify retention before translating.
The last egg is retained in the left pinch. Lift and transfer toward the central holder without rotating yet; move the right arm farther aside.
Approach the remaining cup with a much slower, small tilt while maintaining the closed pinch and clearance; check that the last egg stays between the pads.
The last egg remains retained. Continue the slow approach and gradual tilt toward the back-right cup, with both arms separated.
Finish slow alignment above the remaining back-right cup and begin lowering the retained egg, keeping the wrist left of center.
The final egg is aligned laterally but the lid is close to the fingers. Shift slightly toward the front for clearance, then lower toward the empty cup with the pinch closed.
Downward motion is impeded near the lid. The egg is above the empty cup; open and allow it to settle, then withdraw upward and left without further pressing.
All four eggs are visible in the holder. Clear the left arm and bring the closed right fingers above the rear of the lid for a controlled closing push.

The new view shows the fourth egg resting over the front-right egg, leaving the back-right cup empty. Replan after the continuity rejection: withdraw left and approach the perched egg with the right gripper before closing the lid.
The right fingers are impeded by the lid. Narrow them and withdraw forward and slightly right from the observed pose before attempting a front-side approach to the perched egg.
Approach the perched fourth egg from the front with the right gripper open, staying ahead of the lid and above the three seated eggs.
Lower the right finger pads around the raised egg, with a modest forward correction and narrower opening to avoid the seated eggs, then close.
Lift the pinched fourth egg clear of the seated front-right egg, then begin a small straight transfer toward the empty back-right cup.
The fourth egg is retained. Translate it forward over the empty back-right cup and lower gently, leaving the other three eggs undisturbed.
